Subject: Discovery recap - BrightCart embeddings & reranking (index scale, latency & next steps)

Hi Alex / Priya -

Thanks again for the productive call today. Quick recap of what I heard and next steps so we're aligned. Please reply with any corrections.

Pain points / goals
- Search relevance for product recommendations is inconsistent across long-tail queries; manual tuning in ElasticSearch is getting expensive and brittle.
- Need a reranking layer (embeddings + cross-encoder / reranker) that can improve top-K accuracy without blowing latency SLOs.
- Cost sensitivity: aiming to keep incremental costs for reranking under ~$150 per 1M queries.

Current stack (from our conversation)
- Primary catalog and search: AWS OpenSearch (Elasticsearch).
- Vector store: Pinecone for recent POC.
- Traffic profile: ~1.2M daily active queries; rerank only applied to ~15-20% of queries (top-50 candidate set).
- Index size: ~120M product vectors (512-d), with daily batch reindex and near-real-time updates for new SKUs.

Success criteria (what success looks like)
- Relevance uplift: measurable +5-10% CTR on product recs (A/B).
- Latency: end-to-end rerank P95 < 100ms (preference for < 75ms if achievable).
- Cost: incremental cost for rerank under stated target; predictable unit economics.

Technical constraints / patterns to consider
- We need ability to handle 120M vectors and support frequent small updates (thousands/day).
- Batching: nightly bulk reindex (~10M vectors) plus steady stream of point updates; request pattern includes many small realtime queries and some larger batched offline scoring jobs.

Proposed next steps
1) Redwood trial environment: we'll provision a test index (10M vectors) and run a benchmark with your sample traffic (you mentioned a sample export).
2) Technical deep-dive with Dev (30-45m) to validate latency and batching behavior - propose Dec 3 or Dec 4.
3) I'll send an initial sizing + cost estimate and a one-page mutual action plan after we get the sample traffic.

Attachments: brightcart-discovery-notes.pdf (call notes), brightcart-example-traffic.csv (sample traffic export)

If that captures things, I'll kick off the trial and schedule the deep-dive.

Thanks -
Marissa Cole

Subject: Internal: BrightCart technical notes / benchmark plan

Marissa / Rishi - internal follow-up after the discovery call. Notes for the benchmark and what I'll need from BrightCart:

Quick plan
- Step 1: Load 10M vectors into a Redwood-managed test cluster (match dims 512).
- Step 2: Run single-query latency tests at 1qps-200qps to get P50/P95.
- Step 3: Run small-batch workloads (batch sizes 4, 8, 16) to reproduce their rerank pattern (top-50 -> final top-10).
- Step 4: Evaluate KV cache benefits for repeated prefixes and measure cost delta for quantized vs FP16 vs int8 options.

Data / artifacts requested from BrightCart (ask prior to deep-dive)
- Sample CSV (they already committed) with candidate lists and query timestamps.
- Short schema for candidate payload (ids, features, metadata).
- Expected update QPS for realtime updates (we have ~8k/day point updates, need peak QPS for spikes).

Initial hypotheses
- With continuous batching and prefix caching we can likely hit P95 ~60-90ms for single-query rerank on a 10M test index depending on model choice and quantization.
- Compression (int8 / scalar quantization) might be necessary to keep memory footprint manageable at 120M; need to validate recall impact.

I'll prepare a short benchmarking doc and send to Marissa to attach to the trial.
